compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (Blackwell): high SM count, large register file/SMEM, fp16 tensor cores (wmma/mma). Input dims: B=1,H=720,W=1280,C=32, window=4x4, N=16, heads=1, mlp_ratio=4 -> hidden=128.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Per-window working set is tiny: 16 tokens x 32 channels = 512 fp16 = 1KB activations; weights qkv (32x96), proj (32x32), fc1 (32x128), fc2 (128x32) total ~22KB fp16. Fits easily in shared memory per block; full fusion is feasible.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Tensor-core utilization low at N=16,C=32; mma 16x16x16 fits but limited speedup over CUDA cores at this size.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input/output 1*720*1280*32*2B = ~59MB read + 59MB write. Likely memory-bandwidth bound if fully fused; weights are reused across 720*1280/16 = 57600 windows.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Bandwidth ceiling on RTX5090 ~1.7 TB/s; want to minimize global memory traffic to ~2x input size.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window state: 16 tokens of 32 ch (residual) + qkv intermediates + attn matrix 16x16 + mlp hidden 16x128. Hidden 16x128 fp16 = 4KB per window — fits in SMEM.
register_pressure.risk: Holding full mlp hidden in regs would blow occupancy; use SMEM for hidden tile.

nodes.notes: ANALYSIS: (1) Classification: Fused transformer block (LN+QKV+attn+softmax+proj+residual+LN+MLP+residual) with small window attention. Mixed GEMM + reductions + elementwise. (2) Canonical: per 4x4 window of 32-ch, compute LN, qkv linear (32->96), attn QK^T (16x16) + RPE bias + softmax, AV, proj (32->32), add residual, LN, fc1 (32->128), GELU, fc2 (128->32), add residual. Each window independent. (3) Layout: input (1,720,1280,32) contiguous, can be viewed as (180,320,4,4,32) for windows. Weights small enough to be broadcast/cached. (4) Regimes: small batch (current B=1, 57600 windows) -> memory BW bound; many SMs available; weight reuse high. (5) Knobs: one-block-per-window vs multiple windows per block; SMEM vs register staging of activations/weights; use mma.m16n16k16 for QKV/proj/FC; fp32 accumulation for stability of LN/softmax; vectorize loads as half8/uint4. (6) Skeleton: load 16x32 tile + weights (preloaded into constant SMEM via set_params), compute LN (warp reduce), qkv matmul, attn (small 16x16), softmax (row reduce), AV, proj, add residual stored in regs/SMEM, LN2, fc1->GELU->fc2, add residual, store. (7) Families: A) Full single-kernel fusion per window (TOP, fits comfortably); B) Two-kernel split attn vs mlp (worse, extra global RT of ~59MB); C) cuBLAS-based multi-kernel baseline (simplest, slower). Weights bound via set_params and cached in __constant__ or persistent SMEM.

action.description: Implement a single fused CUDA kernel where each thread block processes one or a few 4x4 windows entirely: load 16x32 input tile into SMEM, perform LN1 with warp reductions in fp32, QKV linear (32->96) using thread-parallel MAC over channels, compute 16x16 attention scores + RPE bias + row-softmax, multiply by V, apply proj (32->32), add first residual, LN2, fc1 (32->128) + GELU, fc2 (128->32), add second residual, write back. Weights stored in __constant__ memory or persistent SMEM populated via set_params(). Use fp16 storage, fp32 accumulation. Vectorize global loads/stores as half2/uint4.
action.rationale: All operations fit in SMEM/regs per window; eliminates ~5 intermediate global-memory round-trips of the reference. Memory traffic reduces to roughly input+output. Weights reused 57600 times so caching is essentially free.
action.title: Full single-kernel fusion (one window per block)

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: does=Single fused kernel; one warp (16 threads) per window, all stages in SMEM with __syncwarp. bottleneck=compute/latency (serial fp32 MACs per thread; QKV/FC1/FC2 dominate).
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes; implements full fusion as intended.
UPDATE_BELIEF: Correctness failed with max_diff=3.01 — likely __syncwarp insufficient across the 2D block (threadIdx.y groups are independent warps only if x-dim=32; here block=(16,WPB) so 4 windows share warps of 32 threads → __syncwarp synchronizes ACROSS windows partially and tokens within a window are split across two warps when WPB=2+). Specifically with block dim (16,4)=64 threads, lanes for win0 tokens 0-15 + win1 tokens 0-15 share warp0; __syncwarp is fine intra-warp but s_attn/s_v reads across tokens of same window need full coverage. The bug is mixing two windows in one warp: token reductions read other window's data via shared indexing but indices use win_in_block so that's fine — however __syncwarp masks all 32 lanes which is OK. More likely: register array `row[N_TOK]` plus heavy unrolled loops cause register spills, but that wouldn't cause wrong values. The real issue: WPB=4 with block(16,4)=64 threads → 2 warps; __syncwarp only syncs within a warp, but each warp contains 2 windows (lanes 0-15 win0, lanes 16-31 win1). Token i of win0 reads s_attn[0][i][*] written by same lane — OK. But the LN/QKV writes to s_x[win][tok][c] and the next stage reads s_q/s_k cross-token within same window — tokens 0..15 of win0 are all in warp0 lanes 0..15, so __syncwarp(0xFFFFFFFF) syncs them. Should work. Need to reduce WPB to 1 or use __syncthreads, and verify rpe_bias layout & qkv weight layout match reference. Debug rounds exhausted (5/5).

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin transformer block at fp16: LayerNorm -> window-partitioned single-head self-attention (window 4x4, C=32) with relative position bias -> proj+residual -> LayerNorm -> MLP (32->128->32 with GELU) -> residual. Input is (1,720,1280,32) fp16 giving 57600 independent 4x4 windows of 16 tokens. Per-window working set (activations + all weights ~22KB) easily fits in SMEM/registers, so full single-kernel fusion is strongly preferred. Bottleneck is global memory bandwidth (~118MB minimum I/O); compute per window is tiny. Key constraints: numerically stable LN/softmax in fp32, RPE bias addition, weight delivery via set_params/pybind, tolerance rtol=atol=0.01.
open_questions: Best block geometry: 1 window/block (1 warp) vs 2-4 windows/block to improve SM occupancy on RTX5090?
Should QKV/proj/FC use mma.m16n16k16 tensor cores or plain FMA given the small shapes and fp16 inputs?
Where to store weights: __constant__ memory (limited to 64KB), persistent SMEM populated per block, or just global with L1/L2 caching?
Is fp16 accumulation sufficient anywhere within tolerance 0.01, or must all matmuls/reductions accumulate in fp32?
Does the evaluator reuse the workspace tensor across runs (does set_params get called once or every iteration)?
Exact LayerNorm epsilon and behavior matching torch.nn.LayerNorm (default eps=1e-5, fp32 stats) — must match.
GELU variant — PyTorch nn.GELU defaults to 'none' (exact erf-based); approximate tanh form would violate 0.01 tolerance only marginally; need to confirm.
